review_items.title: 'In service' proposed for the nine Belmara projects still booked to CWIP: treat a certificate on file as plant in service?
review_items.detail: The nine went into service between May and July and their certificates are on file, $6.8M together, but the plant ledger still books them to construction work in progress until the 6 November close. Accepting the proposal would make 'plant in service' mean 'certificate on file' in every answer, so plant and CWIP balances would stop reconciling to the ledger.

actions.label: Keep plant in service and completed construction distinct
Create a state 'in service = certificate on file'

evidence: Plant_Accounting_unitization_status_2026-10.xlsx: nine projects in service May to July, $6.8M, still in CWIP
psoft.cwip: the nine carry CWIP balances at 30 September
Order 2025-RC-118 §9: plant enters rate base only when in service at the test year end

review_items.title: Seven post-test-year projects dated 2027 → keep CLAIMED_IN the 2026 update because the 28 September schedule shows them on track?
review_items.detail: The schedule of 28 September shows all 38 on track. The in-service file of 12 October dates seven of them in 2027, $41.3M together. The order removes anything not in service by 31 December 2026. Approving would keep the older status and count the seven in the test year.
evidence: BPUC_2026_Post-Test-Year_Schedule.xlsx: all 38 shown on track at 28 September
Inservice_dates_2026-10-12.xlsx: seven dated 2027, $41.3M

review_items.title: Lakeshore June forecasts (15 June round) proposed as current forecasts in the program totals?
review_items.detail: Sixty-three Lakeshore large projects in delivery, $612.4M of approved budget, have no working forecast since 15 June because of the cost tool cut-over. Treating the June figures as current would hide any movement since June, including Dunmoor East, whose manager expects it above 10%.

review_items.title: Spot order lines at Northgate and Ridgeline → mapped to FA-2025-PIPE-01 and FA-2025-VLV-02 because the item codes match: mark them as framework orders?
review_items.detail: Fourteen lines in the 20 October load name an item on Schedule A but were placed with spot suppliers at $0.55M above the framework prices. Matching on item code alone would count them as compliant and the premium would disappear from the measure.
evidence: psoft.po_line: supplier Northgate Supply Co. and Ridgeline Waterworks Supply on listed items
FA-2025-PIPE-01 and FA-2025-VLV-02 Schedule A prices

review_items.title: Depreciation rates from the 2026 study (composite 2.56%) proposed for the test-year roll-forward: replace the approved 2.40%?
review_items.detail: The 2026 study proposes shorter lives for treatment plant and about $2.4M a year more depreciation. It is not filed, and the order says rates change only by order of the Commission. Accepting it would lower the rate base the November update shows.
evidence: Belmara_Depreciation_Study_2026.pdf: 2.56% proposed, not filed
Order 2025-RC-118 §11: 2019 rates stay in effect
Rate_base_working_2026-10.xlsx: approved rates only

review_items.title: Premium avoided by re-placing off-framework lines proposed as a secured saving toward the $24.2M?
review_items.detail: Re-placing the unconfirmed lines on the frameworks stops a premium; it does not lower spend against the baseline the savings program measures. The program counts a saving once it is in an order or a signed contract, and the tracker reports leakage separately.

actions.label: Keep secured savings and avoided premium distinct

pivot.title: 'In service' proposed for the nine Belmara projects still booked to CWIP: treat a certificate on file as plant in service?
pivot.detail: The nine went into service between May and July and their certificates are on file, $6.8M together, but the plant ledger still books them to construction work in progress until the 6 November close. Accepting the proposal would make 'plant in service' mean 'certificate on file' in every answer, so plant and CWIP balances would stop reconciling to the ledger.
pivot.why_pivot: This item changes what a word means, not what a row says. Accepting it silently would make every answer about plant in service count certificates rather than the ledger, and the rate base, net plant and CWIP figures would stop tying to Plant Accounting's books.
evidence: Plant_Accounting_unitization_status_2026-10.xlsx: nine projects in service May to July, $6.8M, still in CWIP
psoft.cwip: the nine carry CWIP balances at 30 September
Order 2025-RC-118 §9: plant enters rate base only when in service at the test year end

options.label: Keep plant in service and completed construction distinct
options.consequence: Answers show the nine as completed construction not classified, beside plant in service, until Plant Accounting moves them on 6 November.

options.label: Create a state 'in service = certificate on file'
options.consequence: Adds a state; plant in service then includes the nine, and plant stops reconciling to the ledger until the close.

nodes.label: Project
nodes.sublabel: A capital project keyed by project_code, with its utility, region, category, stage and manager.

nodes.label: Utility
nodes.sublabel: One of the four regulated utilities, or Shared Services. Each answers to its own state commission.

nodes.label: Region
nodes.sublabel: An operating region that groups business units for project delivery.

nodes.label: Program
nodes.sublabel: A program that groups projects or initiatives: the Federal PFAS Program, the Lead Program, the savings program.

nodes.label: ApprovedBudget
nodes.sublabel: The approved lifetime budget of a project: the Original WIN approval and the Active Budget Plan.

nodes.label: BudgetRevision
nodes.sublabel: A WIN budget revision request, with the level that must approve it.

nodes.label: Forecast
nodes.sublabel: A working forecast at completion from EPBCS: actuals, committed, uncommitted and contingency.

nodes.label: LedgerLine
nodes.sublabel: A posted actual on the PeopleSoft general ledger, by project and period.

nodes.label: Commitment
nodes.sublabel: An open purchase order line: ordered, received, still open, promised date.

nodes.label: Contract
nodes.sublabel: An executed construction or services agreement with its price at award and change log.

nodes.label: ChangeOrder
nodes.sublabel: A change order or amendment with its cost, days and approval.

nodes.label: FrameworkAgreement
nodes.sublabel: A group framework agreement with Schedule A unit prices, mandatory for listed items.

nodes.label: Supplier
nodes.sublabel: A supplier or contractor on an order line or a contract.

nodes.label: RateCase
nodes.sublabel: A rate order or a pending rate case filing before a state commission.

nodes.label: RateBaseComponent
nodes.sublabel: A rate base line: plant in service, accumulated depreciation, deductions and additions.

nodes.label: InServiceDate
nodes.sublabel: The estimated or certified date a project is placed in service.

nodes.label: PlantClass
nodes.sublabel: A plant account class with its gross plant, accumulated depreciation and approved rate.

nodes.label: SavingsInitiative
nodes.sublabel: A procurement saving recorded in the tracker once it is in an order or a signed contract.

nodes.label: Policy
nodes.sublabel: A governing rule: capital program policy, procurement policy, a commission order.

nodes.label: Condition
nodes.sublabel: A dated or numeric condition that qualifies a rule or a decision.

nodes.label: Statement
nodes.sublabel: A dated claim made in a document or a message: evidence, never a record by itself.

nodes.label: Person
nodes.sublabel: A named person who approves, manages or asks.

nodes.label: SourceSystem
nodes.sublabel: A system of record, connected or not.

nodes.label: Measure
nodes.sublabel: A governed measure with a named definition, grain and date basis.

nodes.label: Forecast variance
nodes.sublabel: Forecast at completion minus approved budget, per project, from the latest working forecast. Positive means overrun; a large project above 10% needs a WIN budget revision.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: Large projects above 10%
nodes.sublabel: Large projects in delivery whose forecast at completion is more than 10% above the approved budget, with whether a WIN budget revision is raised.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: Spend vs plan, year to date
nodes.sublabel: Posted actuals in the fiscal year to date divided by the calendarized plan for the same months.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: Annual plan delivery
nodes.sublabel: Posted to date plus the working forecast to year end, divided by the annual plan. Below 95% means capital moves into next year.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: Forecast freshness
nodes.sublabel: Active projects whose latest working forecast is older than 45 days, by region and cost tool.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: Open commitments
nodes.sublabel: Ordered minus received minus cancelled, on open PO lines. Unpaid invoices are not open commitment.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: Change order rate
nodes.sublabel: Approved change orders divided by original contract value, per contract and project.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: Contingency remaining
nodes.sublabel: Contingency still held in the latest forecast divided by contingency at authorization.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: Budget revisions waiting
nodes.sublabel: WIN budget revisions requested and not yet approved, by approval level and age.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: Test-year in-service at risk
nodes.sublabel: Projects claimed in service inside a test year whose expected in-service date is now after the test year ends, with the rate base at stake.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: Plant additions vs rate order
nodes.sublabel: Plant placed in service in the period divided by the capital additions the last order assumed.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: In service, still in CWIP
nodes.sublabel: Projects past their in-service date that still carry an open CWIP balance.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: Program health
nodes.sublabel: Large projects in delivery within 10% of approved budget divided by all large projects in delivery.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: Mandated share of the plan
nodes.sublabel: Planned spend on projects with a compliance driver divided by total planned spend, by vintage.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: Net plant in service
nodes.sublabel: Utility plant in service less accumulated depreciation, by plant class and utility, at a period end.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: Rate base
nodes.sublabel: Net plant in service less contributions in aid of construction, accumulated deferred income taxes and customer advances, plus cash working capital and materials and supplies. CWIP
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: Rate base change since the last order
nodes.sublabel: Rate base now against the rate base the last order allowed, with the plant additions that explain the change.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: Plant additions in the period
nodes.sublabel: Cost placed in service in the period, by utility, plant class and project.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: CWIP balance
nodes.sublabel: Open construction work in progress at period end, by utility and project, excluded from rate base.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: CWIP aging
nodes.sublabel: CWIP balance by months since the first charge; balances older than 24 months are reviewed.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: AFUDC accrued
nodes.sublabel: AFUDC posted in the fiscal year to date, by project.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: Depreciation expense
nodes.sublabel: Depreciation booked in the period, by plant class, at the rates the last order approved.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: In service, not yet unitized
nodes.sublabel: Assets placed in service whose cost Plant Accounting has not yet unitized, by project and age.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: Framework compliance
nodes.sublabel: Spend on catalogue items ordered under a framework agreement divided by all spend on items a framework covers.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: Off-framework price premium
nodes.sublabel: What off-framework order lines cost above the framework price for the same item: (unit price minus framework price) times quantity.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: Savings secured against target
nodes.sublabel: Savings secured since 1 July 2026 against the target of 2.5% of addressable capital procurement spend.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: Framework supplier lead time
nodes.sublabel: Lead time each framework supplier currently confirms, by category.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: Contract growth since award
nodes.sublabel: Current contract value against value at award, per contract.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: Budget revision cycle time
nodes.sublabel: Days from a WIN budget revision request to its approval, by approval level.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: In-service date slippage
nodes.sublabel: Expected in-service date against the date at approval, per project.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: Aged open commitments
nodes.sublabel: Open order lines with no receipt for more than 90 days.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: PFAS program spend against plan
nodes.sublabel: Posted spend on PFAS projects against the FY26 plan for them.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

nodes.label: Forecast movement since last month
nodes.sublabel: Change in forecast at completion between the last two working forecasts, per project.
nodes.source: governed measure register (Capital Program Analyst role)

sanity_checks.question: Which large projects in delivery are forecast to overrun their approved budget by more than 10%?
sanity_checks.verdict: Answerable - at the 15 October forecast, Lakeshore marked provisional
sanity_checks.verdict_body: The walk is Project -> latest forecast -> approved budget -> the 10% condition from the policy. The 63 Lakeshore projects are tested on their June figures and flagged (rq3).
sanity_checks.plan:
MATCH (p:Project)-[:HAS_MEASURE]->(m:Measure {id:'large-over-10'})
MATCH (m)-[:TESTED_AGAINST]->(c:Condition {id:'large_10pct'})
RETURN p, m, c

sanity_checks.question: What is Belmara's rate base at the end of the test year, and how does it compare with the last order?
sanity_checks.verdict: Answerable - approved rates, the seven out, the nine shown as completed construction
sanity_checks.verdict_body: The walk is Utility -> plant by class at approved rates -> rate base components -> the order. The study rates are held out (rq6); the nine are counted as completed construction, not plant in service (rq1).
sanity_checks.plan:
MATCH (u:Utility {id:'BEL'})-[:HAS_MEASURE]->(m:Measure {id:'rate-base'})
MATCH (c:PlantClass)-[:PLANT_OF]->(u)
MATCH (r:RateBaseComponent)-[:COUNTED_IN]->(m)
RETURN u, m, c, r

sanity_checks.question: Which order lines were placed off-framework above the framework price, and what did that cost?
sanity_checks.verdict: Answerable - order line grain, against Schedule A
sanity_checks.verdict_body: The walk is Commitment -> supplier -> the framework that lists the item -> the mandatory condition. Item match alone does not make a line compliant (rq5).
sanity_checks.plan:
MATCH (o:Commitment)-[:PRICED_AGAINST]->(f:FrameworkAgreement)-[:GOVERNED_BY]->(c:Condition {id:'framework_mandatory'})
MATCH (o)-[:PLACED_WITH]->(s:Supplier)
WHERE NOT (f)-[:PARTY]->(s)
RETURN o, f, s

sanity_checks.question: Which projects claimed in the Belmara test year are now at risk of missing it?
sanity_checks.verdict: Answerable - the 12 October in-service file wins over the September schedule
sanity_checks.verdict_body: The walk is RateCase -> claimed projects -> in-service date -> the 31 December condition. The schedule status of 28 September is older evidence and is not used (rq2).
sanity_checks.plan:
MATCH (p:Project)-[:CLAIMED_IN]->(r:RateCase {id:'2026-PTY'})
MATCH (p)-[:FAILS]->(c:Condition {id:'test_year_end'})
RETURN p, r, c
